claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- The name(s) of your child/children
- Their age(s) or date(s) of birth

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're asking about **Alex, who is 18 years old** and lives at home with you.

Since Alex is 18, I need to check whether he meets the requirements for Child Benefit in the 16-19 age group. Let me navigate to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to understand Alex's current situation. For 16-19 year olds, there are specific requirements:

**Is Alex currently in education or training (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

Or if he's recently left education, we'll need to check if there's a special extension that might apply. Please let me know:
1. Is he currently in education or training?
2. If not, when did he leave education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment. He actually left school a few months back.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. So Alex left school a few months ago and is not currently in education or training.

Let me navigate to check if he might be eligible under the extension eligibility rules for young people who have recently left education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check whether Alex qualifies for the 20-week extension that's available for young people who have recently left education.

**Important question: When Alex left school a few months ago, did he register with any of these qualifying services:**
- A government careers service
- Connexions
- The armed services

Also, just to confirm: **Is Alex still 17 years old, or has he already turned 18?**

(Note: The extension typically applies up to age 18, but I want to clarify his exact age and whether he registered with one of these services.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's already turned 18, so he's 18 now. And no, he didn't register with any careers service or anything like that when he left school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex has already turned 18 and didn't register with a qualifying service (like a careers service or Connexions), unfortunately he doesn't qualify for the 20-week extension.

Let me navigate to the ineligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **Alex is not eligible for Child Benefit**.

## Here's why:

Under the UK Child Benefit rules, young people aged 16-19 can qualify only if they are:
1. **In approved education or training**, OR
2. **Recently left education AND registered with a qualifying service** (like a government careers service or Connexions) - but this extension ends at 20 weeks or when they turn 18, whichever comes first

In Alex's case:
- He is 18 years old and left school a few months ago
- He did not register with a qualifying service when he left
- Since he's already turned 18, the 20-week extension period is no longer available to him

## What this means:
Once a young person turns 18 and is not in approved education or training, they generally no longer qualify for Child Benefit (unless they're in specific approved education like A-levels or equivalent, which doesn't apply here).

## Next steps:
If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he enters approved education or training), you may be able to restart your Child Benefit claim. You can contact HMRC for more information or check gov.uk/child-benefit for the latest guidance.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. So basically once he turned 18 and wasn't in college or anything, that's when it stops. Thanks for explaining it clearly - I appreciate your help!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! Yes, you've got it exactly right. Once Alex turned 18 and wasn't in approved education or training, that's when Child Benefit eligibility ended. You've understood the key point perfectly.

I'm glad I could explain it clearly for you. If circumstances change in the future and Alex does enter approved education or training, or if you have any other children you'd like to check eligibility for, feel free to reach out anytime.

Thanks for using this service, and all the best to you and Alex!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you so much, that's really helpful to know. Take care!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and all the best to you and your family! 😊

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Bye! 👋

Now let me record the final eligibility outcome for this assessment:
